functional_semantics.triton: C[b] = A[b] @ B[b] via a (BATCH, M, K) view of A and a (BATCH, N, K) transposed copy of B; output flat (BATCH*M*N,) in A's dtype (impl_triton.py 133-136, 86-97).
functional_semantics.cutile: C[b] = A[b] @ B[b] via (BATCH, M, K) and (BATCH, K, N) views; output c_3d.reshape(-1) in A's dtype (impl_cutile.py 82-84, 52-72, 130).
functional_semantics.note: Both compute the reference torch.matmul(A_3d, B_3d).view(-1) (impl_torch.py 9-12); the result is the same, but the operand layout one side consumes differs (see preprocessing).

stages.triton: Output allocation (134), B^T lookup/materialisation (136, first call only), host descriptors (141/153), one GEMM kernel launch over (ceil(M/tm), ceil(N/tn), BATCH) (impl_triton.py 139-162).
stages.cutile: Output allocation (84), host grid/K-tile arithmetic (118-121), one GEMM kernel launch over (ceil(M/tm)*ceil(N/tn), BATCH) (impl_cutile.py 118-128), flat view return (130).
stages.note: The GEMM stage itself is identical (single launch, full-K per tile). The extra first-call transpose stage on one side is a boundary issue tracked under preprocessing/intermediate_storage.

dependencies.triton: Output tiles independent; sequential K loop inside a program (impl_triton.py 86-94).

reduction_scan_sort.triton: K reduced sequentially in chunks into one fp32 accumulator by tl.dot with accumulator operand; no split-K/atomics (impl_triton.py 84-94).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: K reduced sequentially in chunks (compile-time trip count) into one fp32 accumulator by ct.mma; no split-K/atomics (impl_cutile.py 47-68).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Same reduction structure; grouped/swizzled tile raster on both sides is launch-order only.

precision.triton: fp32 accumulator (84); tl.dot(..., input_precision="tf32") (94); cast to output dtype (96).
precision.cutile: fp32 accumulator (47); operands cast to ct.tfloat32 for fp32 inputs, else native (50, 64-65); cast at store (72).
precision.note: Same precision class, matching the reference's allow_tf32 = True (impl_torch.py 4); config.yaml verify atol 1.0 / rtol 1e-2.

preprocessing.triton: _b_transposed (44-51) materialises B^T = B.view(BATCH, K, N).transpose(1, 2).contiguous() on the first call for a given B tensor object and memoises it in a WeakTensorKeyDictionary (41); run() calls it every time (136), so warmup and timed repeats consume a prepacked (BATCH, N, K) operand without paying the transpose.
preprocessing.cutile: A.contiguous().view / B.contiguous().view (82-83) are zero-copy for the contiguous generator tensors; B is consumed in its given (BATCH, K, N) layout by the kernel (58-62).
preprocessing.note: Genuine F-Q boundary divergence: one side benefits from an untimed, cached pre-transpose that the reference (torch.matmul on row-major views, impl_torch.py 9-11) does not need, while the other side and the reference consume B as given. The contract cannot pick either; the question is stated in review_items and the contract carries a provisional no-repack rule.

intermediate_storage.triton: A (BATCH, N, K) B^T buffer in the input dtype, allocated by _b_transposed and kept alive by the identity-keyed cache for as long as the caller's B exists (impl_triton.py 41-51); plus the output.
intermediate_storage.note: A persistent input-derived buffer that outlives the call exists on one side only; it is the storage side of the preprocessing divergence.

mutation.triton: No input written; output freshly allocated per call (impl_triton.py 134). The identity-keyed B^T cache would serve stale data if B were mutated in place between calls (47-50).
mutation.cutile: No input written; output freshly allocated per call (impl_cutile.py 84).
mutation.note: Neither mutates inputs; the contract forbids mutation. The stale-cache hazard is a consequence of the preprocessing divergence, not a mutation.

hardware_dispatch.triton: _default_config() (27-35) substitutes _CDNA3_DEFAULT_CONFIG, which only lowers the pipeline depth of the non-autotuned path, when detect_arch() == 'cdna3' and the builtin default is in place (17-24); the host TensorDescriptor path is unconditional (123-127).
hardware_dispatch.note: Legality-only resource-fit fallback (shared-memory footprint on gfx942); the algorithm is unchanged and the contract pins nothing.

fq_boundary.note: config.yaml 21-22; assumes square N = K = M as the generator guarantees (tensors.py 88-91). It counts one read of A, one read of B and one write of C. The cuTile boundary matches. The Triton boundary does not: the B -> B^T transpose (an extra read and write of B, impl_triton.py 49) is performed inside run() only on the first call per B object and then served from a cache, so the steady-state timed region consumes a prepacked operand whose preparation is neither timed nor counted and which the reference never performs.

review_items: Decide whether run() may consume B through a pre-transposed/packed layout and, if so, whether that repack must be performed inside every timed call or may be prepared once and cached: the Triton path memoises B^T per tensor identity (impl_triton.py 41-51, 136) so its steady-state latency excludes a transpose the reference never performs, while the cuTile path reads row-major B directly (impl_cutile.py 58-62, 83); the contract currently carries a provisional no-repack, no-cache rule.

Confirm that bytes_expr = 3 * BATCH * M * M * dtype_size (one read of A and B, one write of C) is the intended boundary; the untimed cached B^T materialisation is uncounted, so the Triton column is not comparable to a contract-conforming generated implementation (human_reference_comparable = false) until the first item is resolved or the Triton implementation is changed.

Decide whether the identity-keyed B^T cache (impl_triton.py 41-51), which would silently return stale results if B were mutated in place between calls, should be fixed before that implementation serves as a timing reference.
